title: design tree
description: The plan of a piece of work, at .rn/<yyyymmdd>-<goal>/design-tree.json: the goal, the deliverables, each with the necessary conditions of its best practice in that best practice's order, each necessary condition with its decisions, and the work order. Each deliverable's inputs make the deliverables a tree, each under the deepest deliverable they name. It keeps only what holds now, and git keeps the history of each point.

goal.description: The one end the user is after, which every deliverable serves.

decided.description: The end, as one sentence with the user as its subject, followed by the state its people are in once it holds: what they do then that they couldn't before.

deliverables.description: Every deliverable the goal needs, and a node of each kind that one takes with no file of it in the product. A meta deliverable makes the best practice of a kind that later deliverables have. The list holds no order of the work, which `work` holds.

work.description: The work next, first to last, each after each deliverable that the inputs of what it names name.

by.description: Who settled the point. user: the user decided it. maker: the maker of the deliverable decided it. reasoning: it follows from the goal and the best practices. research: a source found it. The reason itself goes in the commit message that makes the decision.

name.description: The one thing that holds toward the goal once the deliverable exists. It leaves out the path and the kind, which have fields of their own.

path.description: Where the deliverable lies, from the top of the repository: a file, or a folder for a deliverable of many files. For a node with no file, where its file would lie, which names it.

kind.description: The name of the folder of the best practice whose necessary conditions the deliverable meets, such as readme, or `specific` for a deliverable of this product alone, which the check that its `check` names judges.

done.description: A deliverable that meets every necessary condition of its best practice, or passes its check where it's `specific`. It keeps one line: its name, path, kind, and status.

status.description: done: the deliverable meets every necessary condition of its best practice, or passes its check.

open.description: A deliverable not yet done, with the necessary conditions of its best practice and the decisions that answer them.

inputs.description: The path of each deliverable or node this one rests on, read or run, covering each kind that its best practice names in inputs. A path may name a file outside the tree that already exists. The list stays empty where the deliverable rests on none.

status.description: Where the deliverable stands. open: no work on it has started. doing: someone is making it.

necessary_conditions.description: Each necessary condition of the deliverable's best practice, in that best practice's order.

file.description: false for a node of a kind with no file of it in the product: no file is made, its path names it where its file would lie, and its decisions answer each necessary condition of its best practice. Left out for a deliverable whose file the work makes; true is never written.

necessary_condition.description: One necessary condition of the best practice, with whether the deliverable meets it and the decisions that answer it.

id.description: The necessary condition's ID in its best practice, such as N1.

good.description: true once the deliverable meets the necessary condition, false until then.

decisions.description: The decisions that answer the necessary condition, each settled once its inputs exist. The list stays empty until a point of the necessary condition comes up.

about.description: The point of the necessary condition that the decision settles, in a few words.

unsettled.description: A point still open, which the maker asks about instead of guessing.

decided.description: null while the point is open.

specific.description: A `specific` deliverable not yet done, with the check that judges it and the decisions that make it.

inputs.description: The path of each deliverable or node this one rests on, read or run, covering each kind that its best practice names in inputs. A path may name a file outside the tree that already exists. The list stays empty where the deliverable rests on none.

status.description: Where the deliverable stands. open: no work on it has started. doing: someone is making it.

check.description: The check that judges the deliverable, such as a test that passes or an end-to-end test whose key results the records show.

good.description: true once the deliverable passes its check, false until then.

decisions.description: The decisions that answer the necessary condition, each settled once its inputs exist. The list stays empty until a point of the necessary condition comes up.

work.description: One piece of the work next.

do.description: make: a round of the deliverable. decide: settle the point, or put it to the user.

path.description: The path of the deliverable that the work makes, or that holds the point.

condition.description: With decide, for a deliverable of a best practice's kind: the ID of the necessary condition that holds the point, such as N3.

about.description: With decide: the point's about, as the deliverable holds it.
